subject: Physics
title: Laws of Reflection
summary: To hit a hidden target with a laser and a mirror you need 2 rules: i = r (both measured from the normal) and all three rays in one plane.
keyPoints: **First law**: angle of incidence = angle of reflection (i = r).
Angles are measured from the **normal**, not from the surface.
**Second law**: incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in the **same plane**.
Along the normal (i = 0) the ray returns on itself.

blocks.alt: Incident and reflected rays making equal 40 degree angles with the normal
blocks.caption: i = r = 40°, measured from the normal.

list: A ray makes 30° with the mirror: i = 90° − 30° = 60°, so r = 60°.
The angle between incident and reflected rays is 90°: i = r = 45°.
Light falls along the normal: i = r = 0°.

quiz.q: A ray makes 35° with a plane mirror. The angle of reflection is:
Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from:
quiz.explain: Both are measured from the normal.

quiz.q: The angle between incident and reflected rays is 120°. i = ?
quiz.explain: i + r = 120° and i = r, so i = 60°.

quiz.q: The second law says the incident ray, normal and reflected ray:
quiz.explain: All three lie in one plane.

simulation.reason: Swinging the angle and watching r follow i, with the surface angle shown separately, lets students test the law and the common mistake themselves; the target turns it into a challenge.
simulation.objective: Discover that r = i (measured from the normal) by aiming a laser at a target.
instructions: Move the slider to change the angle of incidence.
Watch the angle of reflection and the angle from the surface.
Hit the target, then press New target and try again.
